summary.oneLiner: DiGiSPICE has transformed from an AEPS-focused agent network into a multi-product financial inclusion platform, with UPI Cash Point and agent lending now driving margin expansion and profitability, while regulatory tailwinds around BC banking outlets create a multi-year growth runway.

one-line thesis: DiGiSPICE has transformed from an AEPS-focused agent network into a multi-product financial inclusion platform, with UPI Cash Point and agent lending now driving margin expansion and profitability, while regulatory tailwinds around BC banking outlets create a multi-year growth runway.
financial scorecard: revenue: INR464cr (+4% YoY, distorted by reclassification); EBITDA: INR201cr (+13% YoY, driven by product mix shift); PAT (rptd): INR25cr (+285% YoY); PAT (normalized): INR19.3cr (ex-INR3.3cr labour provision); order book: N/A (transaction-based); net debt: N/A (no debt disclosed)
guidance: revenue growth: >20% YoY for FY27-28; margin: expanding via high-margin products (credit, insurance); order inflow: UPI Cash Point targeting 50% of AEPS volume in 1-2 years; capex/commissioning: minimal (asset-light network expansion)
segment / subsidiary detail: AEPS: INR59,000cr GTV (+15.9% YoY), 18.4% market share; UPI Cash Point: INR100cr/month run rate (March '26), 30-35% market share; BBPS: INR5,700cr GTV (+7.5% YoY), now 13% of collections; Credit Disbursement: INR539.6cr (+2.7x YoY), INR20cr/quarter; Accounts Opened: 1.65M (+1.6x YoY), INR305cr float balance; Insurance: 35K policies sold
growth verticals / optionality: UPI Cash Point scaling to 50% of AEPS volume; Banking Outlet expansion post-June 2026 regulatory clarity; MSME lending via Muthoot partnership; South India agent network expansion; cross-selling FDs/RDs on existing 1.65M accounts
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin expanded to 13% (INR201cr) from 11.5% in FY25 due to higher mix of credit (32-36% interest), insurance, and float income; OpEx efficiency improved via network optimization; credit loss rates stable due to platform-led underwriting
capex / expansion: Minimal; asset-light model; capex focused on tech stack and agent onboarding, not physical infrastructure
capital allocation: Prioritizing reinvestment into credit underwriting tech, UPI Cash Point scaling, and agent subscription products; merger with Spice Money to streamline structure and unlock listing value; no dividends or buybacks mentioned
risks & watch-items: Macro slowdown impacting rural discretionary spending; regulatory delays in BC-BO guidelines; UPI Cash Point adoption lag if major UPI app (1 remaining) delays integration; credit portfolio quality deterioration if repeat borrower defaults rise
management quality / tone: Confident, forward-looking, and disciplined; emphasized profitability, operational efficiency, and flywheel dynamics; acknowledged macro risks but positioned platform as essential infrastructure
non-obvious takeaways: UPI Cash Point is not a new license but a network play — DiGiSPICE’s 1.7M agents are the moat; agent lending is a self-reinforcing flywheel: more transactions → better data → better underwriting → higher loan ticket → more agent stickiness → more transactions; float income from 1.65M bank accounts (INR50L/quarter) is an underappreciated recurring revenue stream

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
